prompt: please write a regex that has a capture group for a phone number and email in the text
response:
To capture a phone number and an email address in a text using a regular expression, you can use the following pattern:

```regex
\b\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}\b|[\w\.-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b
```

This pattern works as follows:

- `\b` matches a word boundary to ensure we capture the phone number and email separately.
- `\d{3}` matches three digits.
- `[-.\s]?` matches an optional hyphen, period, or space.
- `\d{3}` matches three more digits.
- `[-.\s]?` matches an optional hyphen, period, or space.
- `\d{4}` matches four digits.
- `\b` matches a word boundary again to ensure we capture the last part of the email address.
- `|` is an OR operator to match either the phone number or the email.
- `[\w\.-]+` matches one or more word characters, dots, or hyphens.
- `@` matches an at symbol.
- `[A-Za-z0-9-]+` matches one or more letters, digits, or hyphens.
- `\.[A-Za-z]{2,}` matches a dot followed by two or more letters.
- `\b` matches a word boundary again to ensure we capture the last part of the email address.

You can use this regular expression in your code to extract the phone number and email from the text.
